scale.label: 11 µm detail variant
scale.note: log10(1.12e-5) = -4.9508, which rounds to the assigned -4.951

evolutionary_history.what_changes_at_this_scale: The sampled series has a single extant point, so there is no fossil predecessor and no younger successor. The developmental predecessor of the patterned epidermis is the sub-threshold state D_v/D_u = 1, where σ(k_c) < 0 and the activator stays spatially flat. Relative to the organ-scale sibling (Camazine 1991 comb, λ ≈ 5.2 mm), k_c here is about 464 times larger. Those comb parameters are not reused.

state_variables.u: activator concentration, steady value u* = a + b = 1
state_variables.v: inhibitor concentration, steady value v* = b / (a+b)^2 = 0.9

equations.schnakenberg: du/dt = γ (a - u + u^2 v) + D_u ∇²u; dv/dt = γ (b - u^2 v) + D_v ∇²v
equations.dispersion: σ(k) = 1/2 (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) of J - k̂^2 diag(D_u, D_v)

boundary_conditions: periodic on an interior epidermal window, 134.4 µm by 100.8 µm (12 by 9 critical wavelengths)
initial_condition: homogeneous steady state plus N(0, 0.02^2) noise, seed 3115

run_results.pattern: saturated spot lattice at the critical wavelength (Schnakenberg above threshold); not a retuning of the millimetre comb

empirical_claims: Turing 1952: two-morphogen diffusion-driven instability; k_c is the fastest-growing wavenumber.
Schnakenberg 1979: the cubic activator-inhibitor kinetics used here.
Murray 1981: coat-marking prepattern; wavelength set by the ratio of reaction rate to diffusion.

Ribi, Warrant and Zeil 2011: honeybee ocellar rhabdom sheets average 8.7 µm long and 1 µm wide; ventral retinula cells about 25 µm with dense screening pigment; dorsal cells about 60 µm with sparse pigment. This is the nearest published cellular length, not a measured chemical wavelength.
Ogawa, Ribi, Zeil and Hemmi 2017: worker lateral ocelli about 1100 photoreceptors, median about 1350; the retina is split into dorsal and ventral sub-retinae.
Camazine 1991: comb self-organization at cell scale (~5 mm). Cited only as the scale contrast. Parameters are not copied.

reported_in_source: Turing dispersion and the diffusion-driven instability condition

transfer_boundary: No honeybee paper measured a chemical Turing wavelength of 11.2 µm. The length is the assigned detail scale, placed next to the 8.7 µm rhabdom long axis (relative gap 0.287).
